ko.title: [소비자 심리학 #8] 다섯 번째에는 좋아 보이던 광고가 열다섯 번째에는 싫어지는 이유

segments.src: > Seeing an ad again usually makes it feel more familiar and likable, but only up to a point. After that, people get bored or annoyed, and many learn to tune ads out completely.
segments.tr: > 광고를 다시 보면 보통 더 친숙하고 호감이 가지만, 그건 어느 정도까지뿐입니다. 그 이후에는 지루하거나 짜증이 나고, 많은 사람이 광고를 아예 무시하는 법을 익힙니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Advertisers face a basic puzzle: **how many times should someone see an ad?** Psychology gives a three-part answer.
segments.tr: 광고주는 기본적인 퍼즐에 직면합니다. **한 사람에게 광고를 몇 번이나 보여줘야 할까?** 심리학은 세 부분으로 된 답을 제시합니다.

segments.src: The mere exposure effect.** In the late 1960s, psychologist Robert Zajonc showed people things they had no opinion about, like made-up words, Chinese characters, and photos of strangers.
segments.tr: 단순노출 효과(mere exposure effect).** 1960년대 후반 심리학자 로버트 자이온스(Robert Zajonc)는 사람들에게 가짜 단어, 한자, 낯선 사람의 사진처럼 의견이 없는 대상들을 보여주었습니다.

segments.src: The more often people had seen something, the more they tended to like it.
segments.tr: 사람들이 어떤 것을 더 자주 본 경우일수록 그것을 더 좋아하는 경향이 있었습니다.

segments.src: Nobody had to say anything persuasive.
segments.tr: 누구도 설득력 있는 말을 할 필요가 없었습니다.

segments.src: Familiarity alone was enough.
segments.tr: 단지 익숙함만으로도 충분했습니다.

segments.src: One common explanation is *processing fluency*: something we've seen before is easier for the brain to process, and that ease feels pleasant.
segments.tr: 흔히 드는 설명은 *처리 유창성(processing fluency)*입니다. 이전에 본 것은 뇌가 처리하기 더 쉽고, 그 쉬움이 기분 좋게 느껴진다는 것입니다.

segments.src: We often take "this feels easy" to mean "this feels good."
segments.tr: 우리는 종종 “쉽게 느껴진다”를 “좋게 느껴진다”는 뜻으로 받아들입니다.

segments.src: The effect can show up even when people don't remember the earlier exposures, though it's usually strongest for things that started out neutral.
segments.tr: 사람들이 이전 노출을 기억하지 못하는 경우에도 이 효과가 나타날 수 있지만, 보통 처음에 중립적이었던 대상에서 가장 강하게 나타납니다.

segments.src: Wear-in and wear-out.** Repetition doesn't keep helping forever.
segments.tr: **웨어인과 웨어아웃(wear-in and wear-out).** 반복이 영원히 도움이 되지는 않습니다.

segments.src: Researchers describe a two-stage pattern:
segments.tr: 연구자들은 두 단계의 패턴을 설명합니다.

segments.src: - **Wear-in:** The first few exposures help. You notice the ad, understand it, and start to feel familiar with it.
segments.tr: - **웨어인(wear-in):** 처음 몇 번의 노출은 도움이 됩니다. 광고를 알아차리고, 이해하고, 점차 익숙하게 느낍니다.

segments.src: - **Wear-out:** Past some point, more exposures stop helping and can start to hurt. You get bored, start arguing with the message in your head, or feel irritated that it keeps showing up.
segments.tr: - **웨어아웃(wear-out):** 일정 지점을 넘으면 추가 노출은 더 이상 도움이 되지 않고 오히려 해가 될 수 있습니다. 지루해지거나, 머릿속으로 메시지와 논쟁하기 시작하거나, 계속 나타나는 것에 짜증이 납니다.

segments.src: If you plot liking against the number of exposures, you get something like an upside-down U: it rises, levels off, and then falls.
segments.tr: 호감도를 노출 횟수에 대해 그래프로 그리면 뒤집힌 U자 같은 모양이 나옵니다. 올라가다가 평평해지고, 그다음 떨어집니다.

segments.src: Where the peak sits depends on the ad.
segments.tr: 정점이 어디에 있는지는 광고에 따라 다릅니다.

segments.src: Complex or entertaining ads usually hold up longer than simple, loud ones.
segments.tr: 복잡하거나 재미있는 광고는 대개 단순하고 시끄러운 광고보다 더 오래 버팁니다.

segments.src: Advertisers often slow wear-out by running several versions of the same campaign, which keeps the message while changing how it's delivered.
segments.tr: 광고주는 같은 캠페인의 여러 버전을 번갈아 내보내는 방식으로 웨어아웃을 늦추곤 합니다. 메시지는 유지하면서 전달 방식을 바꾸는 것입니다.

segments.src: Ad avoidance.** People don't just sit there and absorb ads.
segments.tr: **광고 회피(ad avoidance).** 사람들은 광고를 가만히 앉아 흡수하기만 하지 않습니다.

segments.src: They push back in three main ways:
segments.tr: 주로 세 가지 방식으로 저항합니다.

segments.src: - **Cognitive:** ignoring the ad mentally. A well-known example is "banner blindness," where your eyes skip right over the parts of a web page that look like ads.
segments.tr: - **인지적(cognitive):** 머릿속으로 광고를 무시하는 것입니다. 잘 알려진 예는 “배너 맹시(banner blindness)”로, 웹페이지에서 광고처럼 보이는 부분을 눈이 그냥 지나쳐 버리는 현상입니다.

segments.src: - **Affective:** forming a negative feeling, such as "I'm sick of this brand."
segments.tr: - **정서적(affective):** “이 브랜드는 질렸다”와 같은 부정적 감정을 형성하는 것입니다.

segments.src: - **Behavioral:** physically avoiding it by skipping, muting, scrolling past, changing the channel, or installing an ad blocker.
segments.tr: - **행동적(behavioral):** 건너뛰기, 음소거, 스크롤로 넘기기, 채널 바꾸기, 광고 차단기 설치 등으로 물리적으로 피하는 것입니다.

segments.src: Avoidance usually goes up when ads interrupt what you're trying to do, when there are too many of them, or when they feel irrelevant to you.
segments.tr: 회피는 보통 광고가 하려던 일을 방해할 때, 광고 수가 너무 많을 때, 또는 나와 무관하게 느껴질 때 늘어납니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you're streaming a show on a plan that includes ads.
segments.tr: 광고가 포함된 요금제로 쇼를 스트리밍한다고 해봅시다.

segments.src: On Monday a 30-second spot for a new $6.99 fast-food breakfast combo comes on.
segments.tr: 월요일에 새로 나온 6.99달러짜리 패스트푸드 아침 세트 30초짜리 광고가 나옵니다.

segments.src: You barely notice it.
segments.tr: 거의 눈에 띄지 않습니다.

segments.src: By Wednesday you know the jingle, and when you drive past that chain's sign on the highway, the combo seems a bit more appealing than it did before.
segments.tr: 수요일쯤에는 그 징글을 외우게 되고, 고속도로에서 그 체인의 간판을 지나칠 때 세트 메뉴가 전보다 조금 더 끌려 보입니다.

segments.src: That's mere exposure and wear-in at work.
segments.tr: 이것이 단순노출과 웨어인이 작동하는 모습입니다.

segments.src: Now say the platform shows you the **same** spot in nearly every ad break all weekend.
segments.tr: 이제 플랫폼이 주말 내내 거의 모든 광고 틈에서 **같은** 광고를 보여준다고 해봅시다.

segments.src: By Sunday you groan as soon as it starts, check your phone until it's over, and may even feel a little less willing to try the combo.
segments.tr: 일요일이 되면 광고가 시작되자마자 한숨을 쉬고, 끝날 때까지 휴대폰을 확인하며, 세트 메뉴를 시도해보려는 마음이 조금 줄어들기까지 할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: That's wear-out, followed by affective and behavioral avoidance.
segments.tr: 이것이 웨어아웃이며, 그다음에 정서적·행동적 회피가 뒤따릅니다.

segments.src: This is why many streaming services and ad platforms have **frequency caps**, which limit how many times one person sees the same ad in a set period.
segments.tr: 그래서 많은 스트리밍 서비스와 광고 플랫폼이 **노출 빈도 상한(frequency cap)**을 둡니다. 정해진 기간 동안 한 사람이 같은 광고를 볼 수 있는 횟수를 제한하는 것입니다.

segments.src: It's also why a big campaign, such as one built around a Super Bowl ad, typically rotates several versions instead of running one ad over and over.
segments.tr: 또한 슈퍼볼 광고를 중심으로 한 대형 캠페인이 하나의 광고를 계속 반복하기보다 여러 버전을 돌아가며 내보내는 이유이기도 합니다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. **Mere exposure:** Familiarity by itself tends to increase liking, especially for things we start out neutral about.
segments.tr: 1. **단순노출:** 익숙함만으로도 호감이 높아지는 경향이 있으며, 특히 처음에 중립적이었던 대상에서 그렇습니다.

segments.src: 2. **Wear-in → wear-out:** Repetition helps at first, then levels off, and can backfire through boredom and irritation. Varying the ad slows this down.
segments.tr: 2. **웨어인 → 웨어아웃:** 반복은 처음에는 도움이 되지만 점차 평평해지고, 지루함과 짜증을 통해 역효과를 낼 수 있습니다. 광고를 바꿔 주면 이 과정이 느려집니다.

segments.src: 3. **Ad avoidance:** People avoid ads mentally, emotionally, and physically, most of all when ads are intrusive, frequent, or irrelevant.
segments.tr: 3. **광고 회피:** 사람들은 광고를 인지적, 정서적, 물리적으로 피하며, 광고가 방해가 되거나, 너무 자주 나오거나, 무관할 때 특히 그렇습니다.

segments.tr: ## ✅ 자기 점검 퀴즈

segments.tr: (참/거짓)** 단순노출 효과에 따르면, 반복 노출이 호감을 높이려면 사람들이 그것을 본 사실을 의식적으로 기억해야 합니다.

segments.tr: (객관식)** 처음에는 매력적이던 광고가 여러 번 반복된 뒤 시청자를 눈 굴리게 만듭니다.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Mere exposure effect:** The tendency to like something more simply because you've been exposed to it repeatedly.
segments.tr: - **단순노출 효과(mere exposure effect):** 어떤 것에 반복해서 노출되었다는 이유만으로 그것을 더 좋아하게 되는 경향입니다.

segments.src: - **Processing fluency:** How easily the brain takes in information. Easy processing often feels pleasant and familiar.
segments.tr: - **처리 유창성(processing fluency):** 뇌가 정보를 받아들이는 속도와 쉬움의 정도입니다. 쉽게 처리되는 정보는 보통 기분 좋고 익숙하게 느껴집니다.

segments.src: - **Wear-in / wear-out:** The early stage in which repetition makes an ad more effective, and the later stage in which more repetition reduces its effectiveness.
segments.tr: - **웨어인 / 웨어아웃(wear-in / wear-out):** 반복이 광고 효과를 높이는 초기 단계와, 더 많은 반복이 효과를 떨어뜨리는 후기 단계입니다.

segments.src: - **Ad avoidance:** Anything consumers do to reduce their exposure to ads, whether cognitive (ignoring), affective (disliking), or behavioral (skipping or blocking).
segments.tr: - **광고 회피(ad avoidance):** 소비자가 광고 노출을 줄이기 위해 하는 모든 행동으로, 인지적(무시), 정서적(싫어함), 행동적(건너뛰기 또는 차단) 형태가 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Frequency cap:** A limit on how many times the same person is shown a particular ad within a set time period.
segments.tr: - **노출 빈도 상한(frequency cap):** 정해진 기간 동안 같은 사람에게 특정 광고가 노출될 수 있는 횟수의 제한입니다.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 – False.
segments.tr: *정답: Q1 – 거짓.

segments.src: The effect can occur even when people don't recall the earlier exposures, since familiarity can work below conscious memory.
segments.tr: 익숙함은 의식적인 기억 아래에서도 작동할 수 있으므로, 사람들이 이전 노출을 기억하지 못해도 효과가 나타날 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Q2 – B.
segments.tr: Q2 – B.

segments.src: A positive response that turns negative after too much repetition is wear-out.
segments.tr: 처음의 긍정적 반응이 과도한 반복 후 부정적으로 바뀌는 것이 웨어아웃입니다.

segments.src: Q3 – A.
segments.tr: Q3 – A.

segments.src: Automatically tuning out ad areas without any physical action is cognitive avoidance, and banner blindness is the classic example.*
segments.tr: 광고 영역을 물리적 행동 없이 자동으로 무시하는 것이 인지적 회피이며, 배너 맹시가 대표적인 예입니다.*

zh.title: [消费者心理学 #8] 为什么第五次看广告你会更喜欢，第十五次却开始讨厌

segments.src: > Seeing an ad again usually makes it feel more familiar and likable, but only up to a point. After that, people get bored or annoyed, and many learn to tune ads out completely.
segments.tr: > 再次看到广告通常会让人觉得更熟悉、更有好感，但这种效果只在一定限度内成立。超过这个点，人们会感到厌烦或恼火，许多人还会学会完全无视广告。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Advertisers face a basic puzzle: **how many times should someone see an ad?** Psychology gives a three-part answer.
segments.tr: 广告主面临一个基本难题：**同一个人应该看到一则广告多少次？** 心理学给出了三部分的答案。

segments.src: The mere exposure effect.** In the late 1960s, psychologist Robert Zajonc showed people things they had no opinion about, like made-up words, Chinese characters, and photos of strangers.
segments.tr: 单纯曝光效应。** 20世纪60年代末，心理学家罗伯特·扎荣克（Robert Zajonc）向人们展示了他们毫无看法的东西，比如虚构的单词、汉字和陌生人的照片。

segments.src: The more often people had seen something, the more they tended to like it.
segments.tr: 人们看到某样东西的次数越多，就越倾向于喜欢它。

segments.src: Nobody had to say anything persuasive.
segments.tr: 这一过程中没有人需要进行任何说服。

segments.src: Familiarity alone was enough.
segments.tr: 仅仅是熟悉感就已足够。

segments.src: One common explanation is *processing fluency*: something we've seen before is easier for the brain to process, and that ease feels pleasant.
segments.tr: 一种常见的解释是*加工流畅性*：我们曾经见过的东西，大脑处理起来更容易，而这种轻松感会让人觉得愉快。

segments.src: We often take "this feels easy" to mean "this feels good."
segments.tr: 我们常常把“这感觉很轻松”当成“这感觉很好”。

segments.src: The effect can show up even when people don't remember the earlier exposures, though it's usually strongest for things that started out neutral.
segments.tr: 即使人们不记得之前的曝光经历，这种效应仍可能出现，不过通常对最初持中立态度的事物最为明显。

segments.src: Wear-in and wear-out.** Repetition doesn't keep helping forever.
segments.tr: 渐入期与疲劳期。** 重复并不会永远有帮助。

segments.src: Researchers describe a two-stage pattern:
segments.tr: 研究者把这一规律描述为两个阶段：

segments.src: - **Wear-in:** The first few exposures help. You notice the ad, understand it, and start to feel familiar with it.
segments.tr: - **渐入期：** 最初几次曝光是有帮助的。你会注意到这则广告，理解它，并开始对它感到熟悉。

segments.src: - **Wear-out:** Past some point, more exposures stop helping and can start to hurt. You get bored, start arguing with the message in your head, or feel irritated that it keeps showing up.
segments.tr: - **疲劳期：** 超过某个点后，更多的曝光不再有帮助，甚至可能产生反效果。你会感到厌倦，开始在脑子里和广告信息争辩，或者因为它不断出现而感到烦躁。

segments.src: If you plot liking against the number of exposures, you get something like an upside-down U: it rises, levels off, and then falls.
segments.tr: 如果把好感度与曝光次数的关系画成图，会得到类似倒U形的曲线：先上升，再趋于平稳，然后下降。

segments.src: Where the peak sits depends on the ad.
segments.tr: 峰值出现在哪里，取决于广告本身。

segments.src: Complex or entertaining ads usually hold up longer than simple, loud ones.
segments.tr: 复杂或有趣的广告通常比简单、喧闹的广告更经得起重复。

segments.src: Advertisers often slow wear-out by running several versions of the same campaign, which keeps the message while changing how it's delivered.
segments.tr: 广告主常通过投放同一活动的多个版本来减缓疲劳，这样既保留了核心信息，又改变了表现形式。

segments.src: Ad avoidance.** People don't just sit there and absorb ads.
segments.tr: 广告回避。** 人们并不只是坐在那里被动接收广告。

segments.src: They push back in three main ways:
segments.tr: 他们主要通过三种方式进行抵制：

segments.src: - **Cognitive:** ignoring the ad mentally. A well-known example is "banner blindness," where your eyes skip right over the parts of a web page that look like ads.
segments.tr: - **认知层面：** 在心理上忽略广告。一个典型例子是“横幅广告盲区”，即你的视线会直接跳过网页上看起来像广告的部分。

segments.src: - **Affective:** forming a negative feeling, such as "I'm sick of this brand."
segments.tr: - **情感层面：** 形成负面情绪，比如“我已经讨厌这个品牌了”。

segments.src: - **Behavioral:** physically avoiding it by skipping, muting, scrolling past, changing the channel, or installing an ad blocker.
segments.tr: - **行为层面：** 通过跳过、静音、划过、换台或安装广告拦截器等方式，在身体上避开广告。

segments.src: Avoidance usually goes up when ads interrupt what you're trying to do, when there are too many of them, or when they feel irrelevant to you.
segments.tr: 当广告打断你正在做的事、数量过多，或与你无关时，人们的回避行为通常会增加。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的例子

segments.src: Say you're streaming a show on a plan that includes ads.
segments.tr: 假设你在一个包含广告的套餐里看剧。

segments.src: On Monday a 30-second spot for a new $6.99 fast-food breakfast combo comes on.
segments.tr: 周一，一则 30 秒的广告播出，推广售价 $6.99 的新款快餐早餐套餐。

segments.src: You barely notice it.
segments.tr: 你几乎没注意到它。

segments.src: By Wednesday you know the jingle, and when you drive past that chain's sign on the highway, the combo seems a bit more appealing than it did before.
segments.tr: 到了周三，你已经会哼这段广告曲了。开车经过那家连锁店的路牌时，这个套餐看起来比之前更诱人了一些。

segments.src: That's mere exposure and wear-in at work.
segments.tr: 这正是单纯曝光和渐入期在发挥作用。

segments.src: Now say the platform shows you the **same** spot in nearly every ad break all weekend.
segments.tr: 现在假设平台在整个周末的几乎每个广告时段都向你播放**同一则**广告。

segments.src: By Sunday you groan as soon as it starts, check your phone until it's over, and may even feel a little less willing to try the combo.
segments.tr: 到了周日，广告一开始你就忍不住皱眉，直到它结束都在看手机，甚至可能对尝试这个套餐的意愿也稍微降低了一些。

segments.src: That's wear-out, followed by affective and behavioral avoidance.
segments.tr: 这就是疲劳期，随后出现的是情感层面和行为层面的回避。

segments.src: This is why many streaming services and ad platforms have **frequency caps**, which limit how many times one person sees the same ad in a set period.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么许多流媒体服务和广告平台会设置**频次上限**，即限制在特定时间内同一个人看到同一则广告的次数。

segments.src: It's also why a big campaign, such as one built around a Super Bowl ad, typically rotates several versions instead of running one ad over and over.
segments.tr: 这也是为什么一场大型活动（比如围绕超级碗广告打造的活动）通常会轮换投放多个版本，而不是让一则广告反复播放。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三句话总结

segments.src: 1. **Mere exposure:** Familiarity by itself tends to increase liking, especially for things we start out neutral about.
segments.tr: 1. **单纯曝光：** 仅仅是熟悉感，往往就会提升好感，尤其是对最初持中立态度的事物。

segments.src: 2. **Wear-in → wear-out:** Repetition helps at first, then levels off, and can backfire through boredom and irritation. Varying the ad slows this down.
segments.tr: 2. **渐入期 → 疲劳期：** 重复起初有帮助，之后趋于平稳，并可能因厌倦和烦躁而适得其反。变换广告内容可以减缓这一过程。

segments.src: 3. **Ad avoidance:** People avoid ads mentally, emotionally, and physically, most of all when ads are intrusive, frequent, or irrelevant.
segments.tr: 3. **广告回避：** 人们会在心理、情感和行为上回避广告，在广告具有侵扰性、过于频繁或与自己无关时尤其如此。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测题

segments.tr: （正误判断）**根据单纯曝光效应，人们必须先有意识地记得自己见过某样东西，重复曝光才会提升他们对它的好感。

segments.src: (Multiple choice)** An ad that seemed charming at first now makes viewers roll their eyes after many repetitions.
segments.tr: （单选题）**一则起初很有魅力的广告，在重复多次后，观众看到它就会翻白眼。

segments.src: Which term best describes this?
segments.tr: 下列哪个术语最能描述这种现象？

segments.src: - A) Wear-in
segments.tr: - A) 渐入期

segments.src: - B) Wear-out
segments.tr: - B) 疲劳期

segments.tr: - C) 加工流畅性

segments.src: - D) Frequency cap
segments.tr: - D) 频次上限

segments.tr: （单选题）你在浏览新闻网站时，视线会自动跳过侧边那些看起来像广告的方框。

segments.src: What type of ad avoidance is this?
segments.tr: 这属于哪种广告回避？

segments.src: - A) Cognitive avoidance
segments.tr: - A) 认知回避

segments.tr: - B) 情感回避

segments.tr: - C) 行为回避

segments.tr: - D) 都不是，因为这不属于回避

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Mere exposure effect:** The tendency to like something more simply because you've been exposed to it repeatedly.
segments.tr: - **单纯曝光效应：** 仅仅因为反复接触某事物，就更喜欢它的倾向。

segments.src: - **Processing fluency:** How easily the brain takes in information. Easy processing often feels pleasant and familiar.
segments.tr: - **加工流畅性：** 大脑接收信息的难易程度。处理起来越容易，通常越让人觉得愉快和熟悉。

segments.src: - **Wear-in / wear-out:** The early stage in which repetition makes an ad more effective, and the later stage in which more repetition reduces its effectiveness.
segments.tr: - **渐入期 / 疲劳期：** 前者是指重复使广告效果逐渐增强的早期阶段；后者是指过多重复使广告效果下降的后期阶段。

segments.src: - **Ad avoidance:** Anything consumers do to reduce their exposure to ads, whether cognitive (ignoring), affective (disliking), or behavioral (skipping or blocking).
segments.tr: - **广告回避：** 消费者为减少广告接触所做的任何行为，包括认知层面（忽略）、情感层面（反感）或行为层面（跳过或屏蔽）。

segments.src: - **Frequency cap:** A limit on how many times the same person is shown a particular ad within a set time period.
segments.tr: - **频次上限：** 在特定时间段内，限制同一个人看到某则特定广告的次数。

segments.tr: *答案：Q1 – 错误。

segments.src: The effect can occur even when people don't recall the earlier exposures, since familiarity can work below conscious memory.
segments.tr: 即使人们不记得之前的曝光经历，这种效应仍可能出现，因为熟悉感可以在有意识的记忆之下发挥作用。

segments.src: Q2 – B.
segments.tr: Q2 – B。

segments.src: A positive response that turns negative after too much repetition is wear-out.

segments.tr: Q3 – A。

hi.title: [उपभोक्ता मनोविज्ञान #8] पाँचवीं बार में आपको विज्ञापन क्यों अच्छा लगता है, और पंद्रहवीं बार तक क्यों नापसंद होने लगता है

segments.src: > Seeing an ad again usually makes it feel more familiar and likable, but only up to a point. After that, people get bored or annoyed, and many learn to tune ads out completely.
segments.tr: > एक ही विज्ञापन को फिर से देखने पर आमतौर पर वह ज़्यादा परिचित और पसंदीदा लगने लगता है, लेकिन एक सीमा तक ही। उसके बाद लोग ऊब जाते हैं या झुंझलाने लगते हैं, और कई लोग विज्ञापनों को पूरी तरह अनदेखा करना सीख जाते हैं।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Advertisers face a basic puzzle: **how many times should someone see an ad?** Psychology gives a three-part answer.
segments.tr: विज्ञापनदाताओं के सामने एक बुनियादी सवाल होता है: **किसी व्यक्ति को एक विज्ञापन कितनी बार दिखाया जाना चाहिए?** मनोविज्ञान इसका उत्तर तीन हिस्सों में देता है।

segments.src: The mere exposure effect.** In the late 1960s, psychologist Robert Zajonc showed people things they had no opinion about, like made-up words, Chinese characters, and photos of strangers.
segments.tr: केवल-संपर्क प्रभाव (mere exposure effect)।** 1960 के दशक के अंत में मनोवैज्ञानिक रॉबर्ट ज़ाजोंक ने लोगों को ऐसी चीज़ें दिखाईं जिन पर उनकी कोई राय नहीं थी, जैसे गढ़े हुए शब्द, चीनी अक्षर और अजनबियों की तस्वीरें।

segments.src: The more often people had seen something, the more they tended to like it.
segments.tr: किसी चीज़ को जितनी बार लोगों ने देखा था, वे उसे उतना ही ज़्यादा पसंद करने लगे।

segments.src: Nobody had to say anything persuasive.
segments.tr: किसी को कुछ भी मनाने वाला कहने की ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ी।

segments.src: Familiarity alone was enough.
segments.tr: केवल परिचितता ही काफ़ी थी।

segments.src: One common explanation is *processing fluency*: something we've seen before is easier for the brain to process, and that ease feels pleasant.
segments.tr: एक आम व्याख्या है *प्रोसेसिंग फ्लुएंसी (processing fluency)*: जो चीज़ हमने पहले देखी हो, उसे दिमाग़ आसानी से प्रोसेस करता है, और वह आसानी सुखद लगती है।

segments.src: We often take "this feels easy" to mean "this feels good."
segments.tr: हम अक्सर "यह आसान लग रहा है" को "यह अच्छा लग रहा है" समझ लेते हैं।

segments.src: The effect can show up even when people don't remember the earlier exposures, though it's usually strongest for things that started out neutral.
segments.tr: यह प्रभाव तब भी दिख सकता है जब लोगों को पिछले संपर्क याद न हों, हालांकि यह आमतौर पर उन चीज़ों के साथ सबसे मज़बूत होता है जो शुरू में तटस्थ थीं।

segments.src: Wear-in and wear-out.** Repetition doesn't keep helping forever.
segments.tr: **वियर-इन और वियर-आउट।** दोहराव हमेशा मदद नहीं करता।

segments.src: Researchers describe a two-stage pattern:
segments.tr: शोधकर्ता इसे दो चरणों वाला पैटर्न बताते हैं:

segments.src: - **Wear-in:** The first few exposures help. You notice the ad, understand it, and start to feel familiar with it.
segments.tr: - **वियर-इन:** पहले कुछ संपर्क मदद करते हैं। आप विज्ञापन पर ध्यान देते हैं, उसे समझते हैं, और उससे परिचित महसूस करने लगते हैं।

segments.src: - **Wear-out:** Past some point, more exposures stop helping and can start to hurt. You get bored, start arguing with the message in your head, or feel irritated that it keeps showing up.
segments.tr: - **वियर-आउट:** एक बिंदु के बाद, और संपर्क मदद करना बंद कर देते हैं और नुकसान भी पहुँचा सकते हैं। आप ऊब जाते हैं, मन ही मन उस संदेश से बहस करने लगते हैं, या इस बात से चिढ़ जाते हैं कि वह बार-बार सामने आ रहा है।

segments.src: If you plot liking against the number of exposures, you get something like an upside-down U: it rises, levels off, and then falls.
segments.tr: अगर आप पसंद किए जाने को संपर्कों की संख्या के मुकाबले ग्राफ़ पर दिखाएँ, तो वह उल्टे U जैसा कुछ बनता है: पहले बढ़ता है, फिर स्थिर होता है, और फिर गिरता है।

segments.src: Where the peak sits depends on the ad.
segments.tr: शिखर कहाँ आएगा, यह विज्ञापन पर निर्भर करता है।

segments.src: Complex or entertaining ads usually hold up longer than simple, loud ones.
segments.tr: जटिल या मनोरंजक विज्ञापन आमतौर पर सादे और शोरगुल वाले विज्ञापनों से ज़्यादा देर तक टिकते हैं।

segments.src: Advertisers often slow wear-out by running several versions of the same campaign, which keeps the message while changing how it's delivered.
segments.tr: विज्ञापनदाता अक्सर एक ही अभियान के कई संस्करण चलाकर वियर-आउट को धीमा करते हैं, जिससे संदेश वही रहता है, पर उसे पेश करने का तरीका बदलता रहता है।

segments.src: Ad avoidance.** People don't just sit there and absorb ads.
segments.tr: **विज्ञापन से बचाव (Ad avoidance)।** लोग विज्ञापनों को चुपचाप बैठकर सिर्फ़ नहीं सोखते।

segments.src: They push back in three main ways:
segments.tr: वे तीन मुख्य तरीकों से विरोध करते हैं:

segments.src: - **Cognitive:** ignoring the ad mentally. A well-known example is "banner blindness," where your eyes skip right over the parts of a web page that look like ads.
segments.tr: - **संज्ञानात्मक (Cognitive):** विज्ञापन को मानसिक रूप से अनदेखा करना। एक प्रसिद्ध उदाहरण है "बैनर ब्लाइंडनेस", जहाँ आपकी आँखें वेब पेज के उन हिस्सों को सीधे छोड़ देती हैं जो विज्ञापन जैसे दिखते हैं।

segments.src: - **Affective:** forming a negative feeling, such as "I'm sick of this brand."
segments.tr: - **भावनात्मक (Affective):** नकारात्मक भावना बनाना, जैसे "मुझे इस ब्रांड से चिढ़ है।"

segments.src: - **Behavioral:** physically avoiding it by skipping, muting, scrolling past, changing the channel, or installing an ad blocker.
segments.tr: - **व्यवहारिक (Behavioral):** शारीरिक रूप से बचना, जैसे स्किप करना, म्यूट करना, स्क्रॉल करके आगे बढ़ जाना, चैनल बदलना, या ऐड ब्लॉकर इंस्टॉल करना।

segments.src: Avoidance usually goes up when ads interrupt what you're trying to do, when there are too many of them, or when they feel irrelevant to you.
segments.tr: बचाव आमतौर पर तब बढ़ता है जब विज्ञापन आपके काम में बाधा डालते हैं, जब उनकी संख्या बहुत ज़्यादा होती है, या जब वे आपके लिए अप्रासंगिक लगते हैं।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: Say you're streaming a show on a plan that includes ads.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए आप ऐसे प्लान पर एक शो स्ट्रीम कर रहे हैं जिसमें विज्ञापन आते हैं।

segments.tr: अब मान लीजिए प्लेटफ़ॉर्म पूरे वीकेंड लगभग हर ऐड ब्रेक में **वही** स्पॉट दिखाता है।

segments.tr: - **केवल-संपर्क प्रभाव:** किसी चीज़ को सिर्फ़ बार-बार देखने के कारण उसे ज़्यादा पसंद करने की प्रवृत्ति।

segments.src: - **Wear-in / wear-out:** The early stage in which repetition makes an ad more effective, and the later stage in which more repetition reduces its effectiveness.
segments.tr: - **वियर-इन / वियर-आउट:** वह शुरुआती चरण जिसमें दोहराव से विज्ञापन ज़्यादा प्रभावी होता है, और वह बाद का चरण जिसमें ज़्यादा दोहराव से उसका प्रभाव घटता है।

segments.src: - **Ad avoidance:** Anything consumers do to reduce their exposure to ads, whether cognitive (ignoring), affective (disliking), or behavioral (skipping or blocking).
segments.tr: - **विज्ञापन से बचाव:** उपभोक्ता द्वारा विज्ञापनों के संपर्क को कम करने के लिए किया गया कोई भी कार्य, चाहे वह संज्ञानात्मक (अनदेखा करना), भावनात्मक (नापसंद करना) या व्यवहारिक (स्किप या ब्लॉक करना) हो।

es.title: [Psicología del consumidor #8] Por qué te gusta un anuncio más la quinta vez y lo odias a la decimoquinta

segments.src: > Seeing an ad again usually makes it feel more familiar and likable, but only up to a point. After that, people get bored or annoyed, and many learn to tune ads out completely.
segments.tr: > Volver a ver un anuncio suele hacerlo resultar más familiar y agradable, pero solo hasta cierto punto. Después, la gente se aburre o se molesta, y muchos aprenden a ignorarlo por completo.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Advertisers face a basic puzzle: **how many times should someone see an ad?** Psychology gives a three-part answer.
segments.tr: Los anunciantes enfrentan un dilema básico: **¿cuántas veces debería ver alguien un anuncio?** La psicología ofrece una respuesta en tres partes.

segments.src: The mere exposure effect.** In the late 1960s, psychologist Robert Zajonc showed people things they had no opinion about, like made-up words, Chinese characters, and photos of strangers.
segments.tr: El efecto de la mera exposición.** A finales de los años sesenta, el psicólogo Robert Zajonc mostró a personas cosas sobre las que no tenían opinión, como palabras inventadas, caracteres chinos y fotos de desconocidos.

segments.src: The more often people had seen something, the more they tended to like it.
segments.tr: Cuanto más veces habían visto algo, más tendían a gustarles.

segments.src: Nobody had to say anything persuasive.
segments.tr: Nadie tuvo que decir nada persuasivo.

segments.src: Familiarity alone was enough.
segments.tr: La familiaridad por sí sola bastó.

segments.src: One common explanation is *processing fluency*: something we've seen before is easier for the brain to process, and that ease feels pleasant.
segments.tr: Una explicación común es la *fluidez de procesamiento*: algo que ya hemos visto es más fácil de procesar para el cerebro, y esa facilidad resulta agradable.

segments.src: We often take "this feels easy" to mean "this feels good."
segments.tr: A menudo confundimos "esto resulta fácil" con "esto resulta bueno".

segments.src: The effect can show up even when people don't remember the earlier exposures, though it's usually strongest for things that started out neutral.
segments.tr: El efecto puede aparecer incluso cuando la gente no recuerda las exposiciones anteriores, aunque suele ser más fuerte en cosas que empezaron siendo neutrales.

segments.src: Wear-in and wear-out.** Repetition doesn't keep helping forever.
segments.tr: Asentamiento y desgaste (wear-in y wear-out).** La repetición no sigue ayudando para siempre.

segments.src: Researchers describe a two-stage pattern:
segments.tr: Los investigadores describen un patrón de dos etapas:

segments.src: - **Wear-in:** The first few exposures help. You notice the ad, understand it, and start to feel familiar with it.
segments.tr: - **Asentamiento (wear-in):** Las primeras exposiciones ayudan. Notas el anuncio, lo entiendes y empiezas a sentirlo familiar.

segments.src: - **Wear-out:** Past some point, more exposures stop helping and can start to hurt. You get bored, start arguing with the message in your head, or feel irritated that it keeps showing up.
segments.tr: - **Desgaste (wear-out):** A partir de cierto punto, más exposiciones dejan de ayudar y pueden empezar a perjudicar. Te aburres, empiezas a discutir mentalmente con el mensaje o te irrita que siga apareciendo.

segments.src: If you plot liking against the number of exposures, you get something like an upside-down U: it rises, levels off, and then falls.
segments.tr: Si graficas el agrado frente al número de exposiciones, obtienes algo parecido a una U invertida: sube, se estabiliza y luego cae.

segments.src: Where the peak sits depends on the ad.
segments.tr: Dónde está el pico depende del anuncio.

segments.src: Complex or entertaining ads usually hold up longer than simple, loud ones.
segments.tr: Los anuncios complejos o entretenidos suelen aguantar más que los simples y ruidosos.

segments.src: Advertisers often slow wear-out by running several versions of the same campaign, which keeps the message while changing how it's delivered.
segments.tr: Los anunciantes suelen frenar el desgaste ejecutando varias versiones de la misma campaña, lo que mantiene el mensaje pero cambia la forma de presentarlo.

segments.src: Ad avoidance.** People don't just sit there and absorb ads.
segments.tr: Evitación de anuncios.** La gente no se queda simplemente sentada absorbiendo anuncios.

segments.src: They push back in three main ways:
segments.tr: Responde principalmente de tres formas:

segments.src: - **Cognitive:** ignoring the ad mentally. A well-known example is "banner blindness," where your eyes skip right over the parts of a web page that look like ads.
segments.tr: - **Cognitiva:** ignorar el anuncio mentalmente. Un ejemplo conocido es la "ceguera de banners", en la que los ojos saltan directamente sobre las partes de una página web que parecen anuncios.

segments.src: - **Affective:** forming a negative feeling, such as "I'm sick of this brand."
segments.tr: - **Afectiva:** formar un sentimiento negativo, como "estoy harto de esta marca".

segments.src: - **Behavioral:** physically avoiding it by skipping, muting, scrolling past, changing the channel, or installing an ad blocker.
segments.tr: - **Conductual:** evitarlo físicamente saltándolo, silenciándolo, desplazándose más allá, cambiando de canal o instalando un bloqueador de anuncios.

segments.src: Avoidance usually goes up when ads interrupt what you're trying to do, when there are too many of them, or when they feel irrelevant to you.
segments.tr: La evitación suele aumentar cuando los anuncios interrumpen lo que estás haciendo, cuando hay demasiados o cuando resultan irrelevantes para ti.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Say you're streaming a show on a plan that includes ads.
segments.tr: Imagina que estás viendo una serie en streaming con un plan que incluye anuncios.

segments.src: On Monday a 30-second spot for a new $6.99 fast-food breakfast combo comes on.
segments.tr: El lunes aparece un spot de 30 segundos de un nuevo combo de desayuno de comida rápida por $6.99.

segments.src: You barely notice it.
segments.tr: Apenas lo notas.

segments.src: By Wednesday you know the jingle, and when you drive past that chain's sign on the highway, the combo seems a bit more appealing than it did before.
segments.tr: Para el miércoles ya te sabes la sintonía y, cuando pasas junto al letrero de esa cadena en la autopista, el combo te parece un poco más atractivo que antes.

segments.src: That's mere exposure and wear-in at work.
segments.tr: Eso es la mera exposición y el asentamiento en acción.

segments.src: Now say the platform shows you the **same** spot in nearly every ad break all weekend.
segments.tr: Ahora imagina que la plataforma te muestra el **mismo** spot en casi todas las pausas publicitarias durante el fin de semana.

segments.src: By Sunday you groan as soon as it starts, check your phone until it's over, and may even feel a little less willing to try the combo.
segments.tr: Para el domingo, te quejas en cuanto empieza, revisas el teléfono hasta que termina y puede que incluso tengas un poco menos de ganas de probar el combo.

segments.src: That's wear-out, followed by affective and behavioral avoidance.
segments.tr: Eso es desgaste, seguido de evitación afectiva y conductual.

segments.src: This is why many streaming services and ad platforms have **frequency caps**, which limit how many times one person sees the same ad in a set period.
segments.tr: Por eso muchos servicios de streaming y plataformas publicitarias tienen **límites de frecuencia** (frequency caps), que restringen cuántas veces una misma persona ve el mismo anuncio en un periodo determinado.

segments.src: It's also why a big campaign, such as one built around a Super Bowl ad, typically rotates several versions instead of running one ad over and over.
segments.tr: También por eso una gran campaña, como la construida en torno a un anuncio de la Super Bowl, normalmente rota varias versiones en lugar de emitir un único anuncio una y otra vez.

segments.tr: 1. **Mera exposición:** La familiaridad por sí sola tiende a aumentar el agrado, sobre todo hacia cosas que al principio nos son neutrales.

segments.src: 2. **Wear-in → wear-out:** Repetition helps at first, then levels off, and can backfire through boredom and irritation. Varying the ad slows this down.

segments.tr: تأثير التعرض المجرد.** في أواخر ستينيات القرن العشرين، عرض عالم النفس روبرت زاجونك على الناس أشياء لم يكن لديهم رأي فيها، مثل كلمات مختلقة وحروف صينية وصور لغرباء.

segments.src: The more often people had seen something, the more they tended to like it.
segments.tr: كلما رأى الناس شيئًا أكثر، مالوا إلى إعجابهم به أكثر.

segments.src: Nobody had to say anything persuasive.
segments.tr: لم يكن على أحد أن يقول شيئًا مقنعًا.

segments.src: Familiarity alone was enough.
segments.tr: كانت الألفة وحدها كافية.

segments.src: One common explanation is *processing fluency*: something we've seen before is easier for the brain to process, and that ease feels pleasant.
segments.tr: أحد التفسيرات الشائعة هو *سلاسة المعالجة*: ما رأيناه من قبل يكون أسهل على الدماغ في معالجته، وهذه السهولة تبعث على الارتياح.

segments.src: We often take "this feels easy" to mean "this feels good."
segments.tr: كثيرًا ما نعامل الشعور بأن "الأمر سهل" على أنه يعني "الأمر جيد".

segments.src: The effect can show up even when people don't remember the earlier exposures, though it's usually strongest for things that started out neutral.
segments.tr: ويظهر التأثير أحيانًا حتى عندما لا يتذكر الناس التعرضات السابقة، وإن كان أقوى عادةً في الأشياء التي كانت محايدة في البداية.

segments.src: Wear-in and wear-out.** Repetition doesn't keep helping forever.
segments.tr: الاعتياد والإنهاك.** لا يستمر التكرار في المساعدة إلى الأبد.

segments.src: Researchers describe a two-stage pattern:
segments.tr: يصف الباحثون نمطًا من مرحلتين:

segments.src: - **Wear-in:** The first few exposures help. You notice the ad, understand it, and start to feel familiar with it.
segments.tr: - **الاعتياد:** تساعد التعرضات الأولى القليلة. تلاحظ الإعلان وتفهمه وتبدأ في الشعور بألفة تجاهه.

segments.src: - **Wear-out:** Past some point, more exposures stop helping and can start to hurt. You get bored, start arguing with the message in your head, or feel irritated that it keeps showing up.
segments.tr: - **الإنهاك:** بعد نقطة معينة، لا تعود التعرضات الإضافية مفيدة، بل قد تبدأ في الإضرار. تمل، وتبدأ بمجادلة الرسالة في ذهنك، أو تشعر بالضيق لأنها تظهر باستمرار.

segments.src: If you plot liking against the number of exposures, you get something like an upside-down U: it rises, levels off, and then falls.
segments.tr: إذا رسمت الإعجاب مقابل عدد التعرضات، ستحصل على شيء يشبه حرف U مقلوبًا: يرتفع ثم يستقر ثم ينخفض.

segments.src: Where the peak sits depends on the ad.
segments.tr: يتوقف موضع القمة على الإعلان.

segments.src: Complex or entertaining ads usually hold up longer than simple, loud ones.
segments.tr: عادةً ما تصمد الإعلانات المعقدة أو الممتعة أطول من الإعلانات البسيطة الصاخبة.

segments.src: Advertisers often slow wear-out by running several versions of the same campaign, which keeps the message while changing how it's delivered.
segments.tr: يبطئ المعلنون الإنهاك غالبًا بتشغيل عدة نسخ من الحملة نفسها، وهذا يحافظ على الرسالة مع تغيير طريقة عرضها.

segments.src: Ad avoidance.** People don't just sit there and absorb ads.
segments.tr: تجنب الإعلانات.** لا يجلس الناس ببساطة ليستوعبوا الإعلانات.

segments.src: They push back in three main ways:
segments.tr: يقاومونها بثلاث طرق رئيسية:

segments.src: - **Cognitive:** ignoring the ad mentally. A well-known example is "banner blindness," where your eyes skip right over the parts of a web page that look like ads.
segments.tr: - **المعرفي:** تجاهل الإعلان ذهنيًا. ومن الأمثلة المعروفة "عمى اللافتات"، حيث تتخطى عيناك الأجزاء من صفحة الويب التي تبدو كإعلانات.

segments.src: - **Affective:** forming a negative feeling, such as "I'm sick of this brand."
segments.tr: - **الوجداني:** تكوين شعور سلبي، مثل "لقد سئمت من هذه العلامة التجارية".

segments.src: - **Behavioral:** physically avoiding it by skipping, muting, scrolling past, changing the channel, or installing an ad blocker.
segments.tr: - **السلوكي:** تجنبه جسديًا بالتخطي أو كتم الصوت أو التمرير بعيدًا أو تغيير القناة أو تثبيت مانع الإعلانات.

segments.src: Avoidance usually goes up when ads interrupt what you're trying to do, when there are too many of them, or when they feel irrelevant to you.
segments.tr: يرتفع التجنب عادةً عندما تقاطع الإعلانات ما تحاول فعله، أو عندما تكون كثيرة جدًا، أو عندما تبدو غير ذات صلة بك.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Say you're streaming a show on a plan that includes ads.
segments.tr: لنفترض أنك تشاهد مسلسلًا عبر خدمة بث تتضمن إعلانات.

segments.src: On Monday a 30-second spot for a new $6.99 fast-food breakfast combo comes on.
segments.tr: يوم الاثنين يظهر إعلان مدته 30 ثانية لوجبة إفطار سريعة جديدة بسعر 6.99 دولار.

segments.src: You barely notice it.
segments.tr: بالكاد تلاحظه.

segments.src: By Wednesday you know the jingle, and when you drive past that chain's sign on the highway, the combo seems a bit more appealing than it did before.
segments.tr: بحلول الأربعاء تعرف اللحن، وعندما تمر بلافتة تلك السلسلة على الطريق السريع، تبدو الوجبة أكثر جاذبية قليلًا مما كانت عليه من قبل.

segments.src: That's mere exposure and wear-in at work.
segments.tr: هذا هو التعرض المجرد والاعتياد في العمل.

segments.src: Now say the platform shows you the **same** spot in nearly every ad break all weekend.
segments.tr: والآن لنفترض أن المنصة تعرض لك **الإعلان نفسه** في تقريبًا كل فاصل إعلاني طوال عطلة نهاية الأسبوع.

segments.src: By Sunday you groan as soon as it starts, check your phone until it's over, and may even feel a little less willing to try the combo.
segments.tr: بحلول الأحد تتذمر فور بدايته، وتتفقد هاتفك حتى ينتهي، وقد تشعر حتى بقليل من عدم الرغبة في تجربة الوجبة.

segments.src: That's wear-out, followed by affective and behavioral avoidance.
segments.tr: هذا هو الإنهاك، يليه التجنب الوجداني والسلوكي.

segments.src: This is why many streaming services and ad platforms have **frequency caps**, which limit how many times one person sees the same ad in a set period.
segments.tr: ولهذا تملك كثير من خدمات البث ومنصات الإعلانات **حدود التكرار**، وهي تحد من عدد مرات رؤية الشخص نفسه للإعلان نفسه خلال فترة محددة.

segments.src: It's also why a big campaign, such as one built around a Super Bowl ad, typically rotates several versions instead of running one ad over and over.
segments.tr: ولهذا أيضًا تُدار الحملات الكبيرة، مثل تلك المبنية حول إعلان في مباراة السوبر بول، عادةً بتناوب عدة نسخ بدلًا من تكرار إعلان واحد مرارًا.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص من 3 أسطر

segments.src: 1. **Mere exposure:** Familiarity by itself tends to increase liking, especially for things we start out neutral about.
segments.tr: 1. **التعرض المجرد:** تميل الألفة وحدها إلى زيادة الإعجاب، خاصةً بالأشياء التي كنا محايدين تجاهها في البداية.

segments.src: 2. **Wear-in → wear-out:** Repetition helps at first, then levels off, and can backfire through boredom and irritation. Varying the ad slows this down.
segments.tr: 2. **الاعتياد ← الإنهاك:** يساعد التكرار في البداية، ثم يستقر، وقد يأتي بنتيجة عكسية بسبب الملل والضيق. يؤدي تنويع الإعلان إلى إبطاء ذلك.

segments.src: 3. **Ad avoidance:** People avoid ads mentally, emotionally, and physically, most of all when ads are intrusive, frequent, or irrelevant.
segments.tr: 3. **تجنب الإعلانات:** يتجنب الناس الإعلانات ذهنيًا وعاطفيًا وجسديًا، وأكثر ما يكون ذلك عندما تكون الإعلانات مقحمة أو متكررة أو غير ذات صلة.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Mere exposure effect:** The tendency to like something more simply because you've been exposed to it repeatedly.
segments.tr: - **تأثير التعرض المجرد:** الميل إلى تفضيل شيء ما ببساطة لأنك تعرضت له مرارًا.

segments.src: - **Processing fluency:** How easily the brain takes in information. Easy processing often feels pleasant and familiar.
segments.tr: - **سلاسة المعالجة:** مدى سهولة استيعاب الدماغ للمعلومات. غالبًا ما تبعث المعالجة السهلة على الارتياح والألفة.

segments.src: - **Wear-in / wear-out:** The early stage in which repetition makes an ad more effective, and the later stage in which more repetition reduces its effectiveness.
segments.tr: - **الاعتياد / الإنهاك:** المرحلة المبكرة التي يجعل فيها التكرار الإعلان أكثر فعالية، والمرحلة اللاحقة التي يقلل فيها التكرار الزائد من فعاليته.

segments.src: - **Ad avoidance:** Anything consumers do to reduce their exposure to ads, whether cognitive (ignoring), affective (disliking), or behavioral (skipping or blocking).
segments.tr: - **تجنب الإعلانات:** أي شيء يفعله المستهلكون لتقليل تعرضهم للإعلانات، سواء كان معرفيًا (التجاهل) أو وجدانيًا (عدم الإعجاب) أو سلوكيًا (التخطي أو الحظر).

segments.src: - **Frequency cap:** A limit on how many times the same person is shown a particular ad within a set time period.
segments.tr: - **حد التكرار:** الحد من عدد مرات عرض إعلان معين على الشخص نفسه خلال فترة زمنية محددة.

fr.title: [Psychologie du consommateur n°8] Pourquoi on aime une publicité à la cinquième diffusion et qu'on la déteste à la quinzième

segments.src: > Seeing an ad again usually makes it feel more familiar and likable, but only up to a point. After that, people get bored or annoyed, and many learn to tune ads out completely.
segments.tr: > Revoir une publicité la rend généralement plus familière et plus sympathique, mais seulement jusqu'à un certain point. Ensuite, les gens s'ennuient ou s'agacent, et beaucoup finissent par ignorer complètement les publicités.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Advertisers face a basic puzzle: **how many times should someone see an ad?** Psychology gives a three-part answer.
segments.tr: Les annonceurs sont confrontés à une question fondamentale : **combien de fois une personne doit-elle voir une publicité ?** La psychologie apporte une réponse en trois volets.

segments.src: The mere exposure effect.** In the late 1960s, psychologist Robert Zajonc showed people things they had no opinion about, like made-up words, Chinese characters, and photos of strangers.
segments.tr: L'effet de simple exposition.** À la fin des années 1960, le psychologue Robert Zajonc a montré à des participants des choses sur lesquelles ils n'avaient aucune opinion, comme des mots inventés, des caractères chinois et des photos d'inconnus.

segments.src: The more often people had seen something, the more they tended to like it.
segments.tr: Plus les gens avaient vu quelque chose souvent, plus ils avaient tendance à l'apprécier.

segments.src: Nobody had to say anything persuasive.
segments.tr: Personne n'avait besoin d'être convaincu par un argument.

segments.src: Familiarity alone was enough.
segments.tr: La familiarité suffisait à elle seule.

segments.src: One common explanation is *processing fluency*: something we've seen before is easier for the brain to process, and that ease feels pleasant.
segments.tr: Une explication courante est la *fluidité de traitement* : ce que nous avons déjà vu est plus facile à traiter pour le cerveau, et cette facilité est agréable.

segments.src: We often take "this feels easy" to mean "this feels good."
segments.tr: Nous confondons souvent « c'est facile à percevoir » avec « c'est agréable ».

segments.src: The effect can show up even when people don't remember the earlier exposures, though it's usually strongest for things that started out neutral.
segments.tr: L'effet peut se manifester même lorsque les gens ne se souviennent pas des expositions précédentes, bien qu'il soit généralement le plus fort pour les choses qui étaient neutres au départ.

segments.src: Wear-in and wear-out.** Repetition doesn't keep helping forever.
segments.tr: Imprégnation et usure.** La répétition n'est pas toujours bénéfique indéfiniment.

segments.src: Researchers describe a two-stage pattern:
segments.tr: Les chercheurs décrivent un schéma en deux étapes :

segments.src: - **Wear-in:** The first few exposures help. You notice the ad, understand it, and start to feel familiar with it.
segments.tr: - **Imprégnation :** Les premières expositions aident. Vous remarquez la publicité, vous la comprenez et commencez à la trouver familière.

segments.src: - **Wear-out:** Past some point, more exposures stop helping and can start to hurt. You get bored, start arguing with the message in your head, or feel irritated that it keeps showing up.
segments.tr: - **Usure :** Au-delà d'un certain seuil, les expositions supplémentaires cessent d'aider et peuvent même nuire. Vous vous ennuyez, vous commencez à discuter mentalement avec le message ou vous êtes irrité de le voir réapparaître.

segments.src: If you plot liking against the number of exposures, you get something like an upside-down U: it rises, levels off, and then falls.
segments.tr: Si l'on trace l'appréciation en fonction du nombre d'expositions, on obtient une courbe en U inversé : elle monte, se stabilise, puis redescend.

segments.src: Where the peak sits depends on the ad.
segments.tr: Le sommet dépend de la publicité.

segments.src: Complex or entertaining ads usually hold up longer than simple, loud ones.
segments.tr: Les publicités complexes ou divertissantes tiennent généralement mieux que les publicités simples et bruyantes.

segments.src: Advertisers often slow wear-out by running several versions of the same campaign, which keeps the message while changing how it's delivered.
segments.tr: Les annonceurs ralentissent souvent l'usure en diffusant plusieurs versions d'une même campagne, ce qui conserve le message tout en changeant sa forme.

segments.src: Ad avoidance.** People don't just sit there and absorb ads.
segments.tr: Évitement de la publicité.** Les gens ne se contentent pas d'absorber passivement les publicités.

segments.src: They push back in three main ways:
segments.tr: Ils réagissent principalement de trois manières :

segments.src: - **Cognitive:** ignoring the ad mentally. A well-known example is "banner blindness," where your eyes skip right over the parts of a web page that look like ads.
segments.tr: - **Cognitive :** ignorer mentalement la publicité. Un exemple bien connu est la « cécité aux bannières » : le regard passe directement sur les zones d'une page web qui ressemblent à de la publicité.

segments.src: - **Affective:** forming a negative feeling, such as "I'm sick of this brand."
segments.tr: - **Affective :** développer un sentiment négatif, comme « je suis lassé de cette marque ».

segments.src: - **Behavioral:** physically avoiding it by skipping, muting, scrolling past, changing the channel, or installing an ad blocker.
segments.tr: - **Comportementale :** éviter physiquement la publicité en la sautant, en la coupant, en faisant défiler la page, en changeant de chaîne ou en installant un bloqueur de publicités.

segments.src: Avoidance usually goes up when ads interrupt what you're trying to do, when there are too many of them, or when they feel irrelevant to you.
segments.tr: L'évitement augmente généralement lorsque les publicités interrompent ce que vous êtes en train de faire, lorsqu'elles sont trop nombreuses ou lorsqu'elles semblent sans rapport avec vos besoins.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: Say you're streaming a show on a plan that includes ads.
segments.tr: Imaginons que vous regardiez une série sur une offre de streaming incluant des publicités.

segments.src: On Monday a 30-second spot for a new $6.99 fast-food breakfast combo comes on.
segments.tr: Le lundi, un spot de 30 secondes pour un nouveau menu petit-déjeuner de restauration rapide à 6,99 $ passe.

segments.src: You barely notice it.
segments.tr: Vous le remarquez à peine.

segments.src: By Wednesday you know the jingle, and when you drive past that chain's sign on the highway, the combo seems a bit more appealing than it did before.
segments.tr: Le mercredi, vous connaissez déjà le jingle, et lorsque vous passez devant l'enseigne de cette chaîne sur l'autoroute, le menu vous paraît un peu plus attrayant qu'auparavant.

segments.src: That's mere exposure and wear-in at work.
segments.tr: C'est l'effet de simple exposition et l'imprégnation à l'œuvre.

segments.src: Now say the platform shows you the **same** spot in nearly every ad break all weekend.
segments.tr: Imaginons maintenant que la plateforme vous montre le **même** spot presque à chaque pause publicitaire tout au long du week-end.

segments.src: By Sunday you groan as soon as it starts, check your phone until it's over, and may even feel a little less willing to try the combo.
segments.tr: Le dimanche, vous soupirez dès qu'il commence, vous consultez votre téléphone jusqu'à la fin et pourriez même être un peu moins enclin à essayer le menu.

segments.src: That's wear-out, followed by affective and behavioral avoidance.
segments.tr: C'est l'usure, suivie d'un évitement affectif et comportemental.

segments.src: This is why many streaming services and ad platforms have **frequency caps**, which limit how many times one person sees the same ad in a set period.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi de nombreux services de streaming et plateformes publicitaires appliquent des **plafonds de fréquence**, qui limitent le nombre de fois où une même personne voit la même publicité sur une période donnée.

segments.src: It's also why a big campaign, such as one built around a Super Bowl ad, typically rotates several versions instead of running one ad over and over.
segments.tr: C'est aussi pourquoi une grande campagne, comme celle construite autour d'une publicité du Super Bowl, fait généralement alterner plusieurs versions au lieu de diffuser une seule publicité en boucle.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Résumé en 3 lignes

segments.src: 1. **Mere exposure:** Familiarity by itself tends to increase liking, especially for things we start out neutral about.
segments.tr: 1. **Simple exposition :** la familiarité seule tend à accroître l'appréciation, surtout pour les choses qui nous laissaient neutres au départ.

segments.src: 2. **Wear-in → wear-out:** Repetition helps at first, then levels off, and can backfire through boredom and irritation. Varying the ad slows this down.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termes du jour

segments.src: - **Mere exposure effect:** The tendency to like something more simply because you've been exposed to it repeatedly.
segments.tr: - **Effet de simple exposition :** la tendance à apprécier davantage quelque chose simplement parce qu'on y a été exposé de manière répétée.

segments.src: - **Processing fluency:** How easily the brain takes in information. Easy processing often feels pleasant and familiar.
segments.tr: - **Fluidité de traitement :** la facilité avec laquelle le cerveau assimile une information. Un traitement facile est souvent perçu comme agréable et familier.

segments.src: - **Wear-in / wear-out:** The early stage in which repetition makes an ad more effective, and the later stage in which more repetition reduces its effectiveness.
segments.tr: - **Imprégnation / usure :** la phase initiale où la répétition rend une publicité plus efficace, et la phase ultérieure où une répétition supplémentaire réduit son efficacité.

segments.src: - **Ad avoidance:** Anything consumers do to reduce their exposure to ads, whether cognitive (ignoring), affective (disliking), or behavioral (skipping or blocking).
segments.tr: - **Évitement de la publicité :** tout ce que font les consommateurs pour réduire leur exposition aux publicités, qu'il s'agisse d'un évitement cognitif (ignorer), affectif (rejeter) ou comportemental (sauter ou bloquer).

segments.src: - **Frequency cap:** A limit on how many times the same person is shown a particular ad within a set time period.
segments.tr: - **Plafond de fréquence :** une limite au nombre de fois où une même personne peut être exposée à une publicité donnée sur une période déterminée.

pt.title: [Psicologia do Consumidor #8] Por que você gosta mais de um anúncio na quinta vez e o odeia na décima quinta

segments.src: > Seeing an ad again usually makes it feel more familiar and likable, but only up to a point. After that, people get bored or annoyed, and many learn to tune ads out completely.
segments.tr: > Rever um anúncio geralmente o torna mais familiar e simpático, mas só até certo ponto. Depois disso, as pessoas se cansam ou se irritam, e muitas aprendem a ignorar os anúncios por completo.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de hoje

segments.src: Advertisers face a basic puzzle: **how many times should someone see an ad?** Psychology gives a three-part answer.
segments.tr: Anunciantes enfrentam um dilema básico: **quantas vezes alguém deve ver um anúncio?** A psicologia oferece uma resposta em três partes.

segments.src: The mere exposure effect.** In the late 1960s, psychologist Robert Zajonc showed people things they had no opinion about, like made-up words, Chinese characters, and photos of strangers.
segments.tr: **O efeito da mera exposição.** No fim da década de 1960, o psicólogo Robert Zajonc mostrou a pessoas coisas sobre as quais elas não tinham opinião, como palavras inventadas, caracteres chineses e fotos de desconhecidos.

segments.src: The more often people had seen something, the more they tended to like it.
segments.tr: Quanto mais vezes as pessoas tinham visto algo, mais tendiam a gostar dele.

segments.src: Nobody had to say anything persuasive.
segments.tr: Ninguém precisava dizer nada persuasivo.

segments.src: Familiarity alone was enough.
segments.tr: A familiaridade, por si só, bastava.

segments.src: One common explanation is *processing fluency*: something we've seen before is easier for the brain to process, and that ease feels pleasant.
segments.tr: Uma explicação comum é a *fluência de processamento*: algo que já vimos é mais fácil para o cérebro processar, e essa facilidade parece agradável.

segments.src: We often take "this feels easy" to mean "this feels good."
segments.tr: Muitas vezes tomamos “isso é fácil” como sinônimo de “isso é bom”.

segments.src: The effect can show up even when people don't remember the earlier exposures, though it's usually strongest for things that started out neutral.
segments.tr: O efeito pode aparecer mesmo quando as pessoas não se lembram das exposições anteriores, embora costume ser mais forte em coisas que começaram neutras.

segments.src: Wear-in and wear-out.** Repetition doesn't keep helping forever.
segments.tr: Wear-in e wear-out.** A repetição não continua ajudando para sempre.

segments.src: Researchers describe a two-stage pattern:
segments.tr: Pesquisadores descrevem um padrão em duas etapas:

segments.src: - **Wear-in:** The first few exposures help. You notice the ad, understand it, and start to feel familiar with it.
segments.tr: - **Wear-in:** As primeiras exposições ajudam. Você percebe o anúncio, entende e começa a se sentir familiarizado com ele.

segments.src: - **Wear-out:** Past some point, more exposures stop helping and can start to hurt. You get bored, start arguing with the message in your head, or feel irritated that it keeps showing up.
segments.tr: - **Wear-out:** Depois de certo ponto, mais exposições deixam de ajudar e podem começar a atrapalhar. Você se entedia, começa a discutir mentalmente com a mensagem ou fica irritado por ela aparecer o tempo todo.

segments.src: If you plot liking against the number of exposures, you get something like an upside-down U: it rises, levels off, and then falls.
segments.tr: Se você representar a simpatia em função do número de exposições, obtém algo como um U invertido: sobe, estabiliza e depois cai.

segments.src: Where the peak sits depends on the ad.
segments.tr: Onde está o pico depende do anúncio.

segments.src: Complex or entertaining ads usually hold up longer than simple, loud ones.
segments.tr: Anúncios complexos ou divertidos costumam aguentar mais tempo do que os simples e barulhentos.

segments.src: Advertisers often slow wear-out by running several versions of the same campaign, which keeps the message while changing how it's delivered.
segments.tr: Anunciantes frequentemente retardam o wear-out rodando várias versões da mesma campanha, o que mantém a mensagem e muda a forma como ela é apresentada.

segments.src: Ad avoidance.** People don't just sit there and absorb ads.
segments.tr: Evitação de anúncios.** As pessoas não ficam simplesmente absorvendo anúncios.

segments.src: They push back in three main ways:
segments.tr: Elas reagem de três maneiras principais:

segments.src: - **Cognitive:** ignoring the ad mentally. A well-known example is "banner blindness," where your eyes skip right over the parts of a web page that look like ads.
segments.tr: - **Cognitiva:** ignorar o anúncio mentalmente. Um exemplo conhecido é a “cegueira de banner” (*banner blindness*), em que os olhos passam direto pelas partes de uma página da web que parecem anúncios.

segments.src: - **Affective:** forming a negative feeling, such as "I'm sick of this brand."
segments.tr: - **Afetiva:** formar um sentimento negativo, como “estou cansado desta marca”.

segments.src: - **Behavioral:** physically avoiding it by skipping, muting, scrolling past, changing the channel, or installing an ad blocker.
segments.tr: - **Comportamental:** evitar fisicamente, pulando, silenciando, rolando a tela, trocando de canal ou instalando um bloqueador de anúncios.

segments.src: Avoidance usually goes up when ads interrupt what you're trying to do, when there are too many of them, or when they feel irrelevant to you.
segments.tr: A evitação costuma aumentar quando os anúncios interrompem o que você está fazendo, quando são muitos ou quando parecem irrelevantes para você.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## No dia a dia

segments.src: Say you're streaming a show on a plan that includes ads.
segments.tr: Imagine que você está assistindo a uma série em um plano com anúncios.

segments.src: On Monday a 30-second spot for a new $6.99 fast-food breakfast combo comes on.
segments.tr: Na segunda-feira, aparece um comercial de 30 segundos de um novo combo de café da manhã de fast-food por US$ 6,99.

segments.src: You barely notice it.
segments.tr: Você mal percebe.

segments.src: By Wednesday you know the jingle, and when you drive past that chain's sign on the highway, the combo seems a bit more appealing than it did before.
segments.tr: Na quarta-feira, você já sabe o jingle, e, quando passa pela placa da rede na estrada, o combo parece um pouco mais atraente do que antes.

segments.src: That's mere exposure and wear-in at work.
segments.tr: Isso é a mera exposição e o wear-in em ação.

segments.src: Now say the platform shows you the **same** spot in nearly every ad break all weekend.
segments.tr: Agora imagine que a plataforma mostre o **mesmo** comercial em quase todos os intervalos durante o fim de semana.

segments.src: By Sunday you groan as soon as it starts, check your phone until it's over, and may even feel a little less willing to try the combo.
segments.tr: No domingo, você reclama assim que ele começa, verifica o celular até terminar e talvez fique um pouco menos disposto a experimentar o combo.

segments.src: That's wear-out, followed by affective and behavioral avoidance.
segments.tr: Esse é o wear-out, seguido de evitação afetiva e comportamental.

segments.src: This is why many streaming services and ad platforms have **frequency caps**, which limit how many times one person sees the same ad in a set period.
segments.tr: É por isso que muitos serviços de streaming e plataformas de anúncios usam **limites de frequência**, que restringem quantas vezes uma mesma pessoa vê o mesmo anúncio em um período determinado.

segments.src: It's also why a big campaign, such as one built around a Super Bowl ad, typically rotates several versions instead of running one ad over and over.
segments.tr: Também é por isso que uma grande campanha, como a de um anúncio do Super Bowl, normalmente alterna várias versões em vez de exibir um único anúncio repetidamente.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumo em 3 linhas

segments.src: 1. **Mere exposure:** Familiarity by itself tends to increase liking, especially for things we start out neutral about.
segments.tr: 1. **Mera exposição:** a familiaridade, por si só, tende a aumentar a simpatia, especialmente por coisas sobre as quais começamos neutros.

segments.src: 2. **Wear-in → wear-out:** Repetition helps at first, then levels off, and can backfire through boredom and irritation. Varying the ad slows this down.
segments.tr: 2. **Wear-in → wear-out:** a repetição ajuda no início, depois estabiliza e pode sair pela culatra por causa do tédio e da irritação. Variar o anúncio retarda esse processo.

segments.src: 3. **Ad avoidance:** People avoid ads mentally, emotionally, and physically, most of all when ads are intrusive, frequent, or irrelevant.
segments.tr: 3. **Evitação de anúncios:** as pessoas evitam anúncios mental, emocional e fisicamente, sobretudo quando eles são invasivos, frequentes ou irrelevantes.

ja.title: [消費者心理学 #8] 5回目では好きだった広告が、15回目には嫌いになる理由

segments.src: > Seeing an ad again usually makes it feel more familiar and likable, but only up to a point. After that, people get bored or annoyed, and many learn to tune ads out completely.
segments.tr: > 広告を再び目にすると、たいてい親しみが増し、好感も高まります。ただし、それにも限度があります。その先では人は飽きたり苛立ったりし、広告を完全に無視することを覚える人も少なくありません。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日の概念

segments.src: Advertisers face a basic puzzle: **how many times should someone see an ad?** Psychology gives a three-part answer.
segments.tr: 広告主には基本的な問いがあります。**広告は何回見せるべきか？** 心理学はこれに三つの部分からなる答えを示しています。

segments.src: The mere exposure effect.** In the late 1960s, psychologist Robert Zajonc showed people things they had no opinion about, like made-up words, Chinese characters, and photos of strangers.
segments.tr: 単純接触効果。** 1960年代後半、心理学者ロバート・ザイオンスは、人々に特に意見のないもの、たとえば作り上げた単語、漢字、見知らぬ人の写真などを見せました。

segments.src: The more often people had seen something, the more they tended to like it.
segments.tr: 人がそれを見る回数が多いほど、そのものを好ましく感じる傾向が強まりました。

segments.src: Nobody had to say anything persuasive.
segments.tr: 誰かが説得力のある言葉を発する必要はありませんでした。

segments.src: Familiarity alone was enough.
segments.tr: 単なる親しみやすさだけで十分でした。

segments.src: One common explanation is *processing fluency*: something we've seen before is easier for the brain to process, and that ease feels pleasant.
segments.tr: よくある説明の一つが*処理流暢性*です。以前に見たものは脳が処理しやすく、その処理のしやすさが心地よく感じられるのです。

segments.src: We often take "this feels easy" to mean "this feels good."
segments.tr: 私たちは「わかりやすい」を「好ましい」と受け取ることが多いのです。

segments.src: The effect can show up even when people don't remember the earlier exposures, though it's usually strongest for things that started out neutral.
segments.tr: この効果は、以前の接触を本人が覚えていない場合にも現れることがありますが、もともと中立的だったものに対して最も強く現れるのが通常です。

segments.src: Wear-in and wear-out.** Repetition doesn't keep helping forever.
segments.tr: ウェアインとウェアアウト。** 繰り返しは永遠に効果を高め続けるわけではありません。

segments.src: Researchers describe a two-stage pattern:
segments.tr: 研究者たちは二段階のパターンを説明しています。

segments.src: - **Wear-in:** The first few exposures help. You notice the ad, understand it, and start to feel familiar with it.
segments.tr: - **ウェアイン:** 最初の数回の接触は効果があります。広告に気づき、内容を理解し、親しみを感じ始めます。

segments.src: - **Wear-out:** Past some point, more exposures stop helping and can start to hurt. You get bored, start arguing with the message in your head, or feel irritated that it keeps showing up.
segments.tr: - **ウェアアウト:** ある地点を過ぎると、接触を重ねても効果はなくなり、むしろ逆効果になることがあります。飽きたり、頭の中でメッセージに反論し始めたり、何度も出てくることに苛立ったりするようになります。

segments.src: If you plot liking against the number of exposures, you get something like an upside-down U: it rises, levels off, and then falls.
segments.tr: 接触回数に対する好感度をグラフにすると、逆U字のような形になります。上がり、横ばいになり、やがて下がります。

segments.src: Where the peak sits depends on the ad.
segments.tr: ピークがどこにくるかは広告によって異なります。

segments.src: Complex or entertaining ads usually hold up longer than simple, loud ones.
segments.tr: 複雑な広告や面白い広告は、単純で大声を上げるような広告より長持ちするのが普通です。

segments.src: Advertisers often slow wear-out by running several versions of the same campaign, which keeps the message while changing how it's delivered.
segments.tr: 広告主は、同じキャンペーンの複数のバージョンを流すことでウェアアウトを遅らせることがよくあります。メッセージは保ちながら、伝え方を変えるのです。

segments.src: Ad avoidance.** People don't just sit there and absorb ads.
segments.tr: 広告回避。** 人は広告をただ座って受け身で吸収するわけではありません。

segments.src: They push back in three main ways:
segments.tr: 主に三つの方法で抵抗します。

segments.src: - **Cognitive:** ignoring the ad mentally. A well-known example is "banner blindness," where your eyes skip right over the parts of a web page that look like ads.
segments.tr: - **認知的回避:** 広告を頭の中で無視すること。よく知られた例が「バナーブラインドネス」で、ウェブページのうち広告に見える部分を目が素通りしてしまう現象です。

segments.src: - **Affective:** forming a negative feeling, such as "I'm sick of this brand."
segments.tr: - **感情的回避:** 「このブランドにはうんざりだ」といった否定的な感情を抱くこと。

segments.src: - **Behavioral:** physically avoiding it by skipping, muting, scrolling past, changing the channel, or installing an ad blocker.
segments.tr: - **行動的回避:** スキップ、ミュート、スクロールで飛ばす、チャンネルを変える、広告ブロッカーを入れるなど、物理的に避けること。

segments.src: Avoidance usually goes up when ads interrupt what you're trying to do, when there are too many of them, or when they feel irrelevant to you.
segments.tr: 広告回避は、広告が自分のしたいことを邪魔するとき、広告の数が多すぎるとき、自分に関係がないと感じられるときに高まる傾向があります。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活では

segments.src: Say you're streaming a show on a plan that includes ads.
segments.tr: 広告付きプランで番組をストリーミング視聴しているとしましょう。

segments.src: On Monday a 30-second spot for a new $6.99 fast-food breakfast combo comes on.
segments.tr: 月曜日、新しい6.99ドルのファストフード朝食セットの30秒スポットが流れます。

segments.src: You barely notice it.
segments.tr: あなたはほとんど気にとめません。

segments.src: By Wednesday you know the jingle, and when you drive past that chain's sign on the highway, the combo seems a bit more appealing than it did before.
segments.tr: 水曜日には、そのジングルを覚えてしまっています。そして高速道路でその店の看板の前を通ると、セットが以前より少し魅力的に見えます。

segments.src: That's mere exposure and wear-in at work.
segments.tr: これが単純接触効果とウェアインの働きです。

segments.src: Now say the platform shows you the **same** spot in nearly every ad break all weekend.
segments.tr: さて、プラットフォームが週末中、ほぼすべての広告枠で**同じ**スポットを流すとしましょう。

segments.src: By Sunday you groan as soon as it starts, check your phone until it's over, and may even feel a little less willing to try the combo.
segments.tr: 日曜日には、広告が始まった瞬間にうんざりして、終わるまでスマホを見て過ごし、そのセットを試してみる意欲が少し下がっているかもしれません。

segments.src: That's wear-out, followed by affective and behavioral avoidance.
segments.tr: これがウェアアウトであり、その後に感情的回避と行動的回避が続きます。

segments.src: This is why many streaming services and ad platforms have **frequency caps**, which limit how many times one person sees the same ad in a set period.
segments.tr: だからこそ多くのストリーミングサービスや広告プラットフォームは**フリークエンシーキャップ**を設けています。これは、一定期間に同じ人が同じ広告を見る回数を制限する仕組みです。

segments.src: It's also why a big campaign, such as one built around a Super Bowl ad, typically rotates several versions instead of running one ad over and over.
segments.tr: また、スーパーボウルの広告を中心に据えた大型キャンペーンでも、一つの広告を繰り返し流すのではなく、通常は複数のバージョンを入れ替えて流します。

segments.src: Advertisers often slow wear-out by running several versions of the same campaign, which keeps the message while changing how it's delivered.
segments.tr: Werbetreibende verlangsamen den Wear-out oft, indem sie mehrere Versionen derselben Kampagne schalten. So bleibt die Botschaft gleich, während sich ihre Darstellung ändert.

segments.src: Ad avoidance.** People don't just sit there and absorb ads.
segments.tr: Werbevermeidung.** Menschen sitzen Werbung nicht einfach nur passiv aus.

segments.src: They push back in three main ways:
segments.tr: Sie wehren sich vor allem auf drei Arten:

segments.src: - **Cognitive:** ignoring the ad mentally. A well-known example is "banner blindness," where your eyes skip right over the parts of a web page that look like ads.
segments.tr: - **Kognitiv:** Die Werbung gedanklich ignorieren. Ein bekanntes Beispiel ist die „Banner-Blindheit“: Der Blick überspringt genau die Teile einer Webseite, die wie Werbung aussehen.

segments.src: - **Affective:** forming a negative feeling, such as "I'm sick of this brand."
segments.tr: - **Affektiv:** Eine negative Haltung entwickeln, etwa „Diese Marke habe ich satt“.

segments.src: - **Behavioral:** physically avoiding it by skipping, muting, scrolling past, changing the channel, or installing an ad blocker.
segments.tr: - **Verhaltensbezogen:** Werbung körperlich meiden, etwa durch Überspringen, Stummschalten, Wegscrollen, Kanalwechsel oder einen Werbeblocker.

segments.src: Avoidance usually goes up when ads interrupt what you're trying to do, when there are too many of them, or when they feel irrelevant to you.
segments.tr: Vermeidung nimmt meist zu, wenn Werbung unterbricht, was man gerade tun will, wenn es zu viel davon gibt oder wenn sie irrelevant wirkt.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Say you're streaming a show on a plan that includes ads.
segments.tr: Angenommen, Sie streamen eine Serie mit einem Tarif, der Werbung enthält.

segments.src: On Monday a 30-second spot for a new $6.99 fast-food breakfast combo comes on.
segments.tr: Am Montag läuft ein 30-Sekunden-Spot für ein neues Frühstücksmenü eines Fast-Food-Restaurants für 6,99 $.

segments.src: You barely notice it.
segments.tr: Sie nehmen ihn kaum wahr.

segments.src: By Wednesday you know the jingle, and when you drive past that chain's sign on the highway, the combo seems a bit more appealing than it did before.
segments.tr: Bis Mittwoch kennen Sie den Jingle, und wenn Sie auf der Autobahn am Schild dieser Kette vorbeifahren, wirkt das Menü etwas ansprechender als vorher.

segments.src: That's mere exposure and wear-in at work.
segments.tr: Hier wirken Mere-Exposure-Effekt und Wear-in.

segments.src: Now say the platform shows you the **same** spot in nearly every ad break all weekend.
segments.tr: Nun stellen Sie sich vor, die Plattform zeigt Ihnen am ganzen Wochenende in fast jeder Werbepause **denselben** Spot.

segments.src: By Sunday you groan as soon as it starts, check your phone until it's over, and may even feel a little less willing to try the combo.
segments.tr: Bis Sonntag stöhnen Sie, sobald er beginnt, prüfen Ihr Handy, bis er vorbei ist, und sind vielleicht sogar etwas weniger bereit, das Menü auszuprobieren.

segments.src: That's wear-out, followed by affective and behavioral avoidance.
segments.tr: Das ist Wear-out, gefolgt von affektiver und verhaltensbezogener Vermeidung.

segments.src: This is why many streaming services and ad platforms have **frequency caps**, which limit how many times one person sees the same ad in a set period.
segments.tr: Deshalb setzen viele Streamingdienste und Werbeplattformen auf **Frequenzbegrenzungen** (Frequency Caps), die begrenzen, wie oft dieselbe Person dieselbe Werbung in einem bestimmten Zeitraum sehen darf.

segments.src: It's also why a big campaign, such as one built around a Super Bowl ad, typically rotates several versions instead of running one ad over and over.
segments.tr: Aus diesem Grund rotieren große Kampagnen, etwa eine rund um einen Super-Bowl-Spot, meist mehrere Versionen, statt eine einzige Werbung immer wieder zu zeigen.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in 3 Zeilen

segments.src: 1. **Mere exposure:** Familiarity by itself tends to increase liking, especially for things we start out neutral about.
segments.tr: 1. **Mere Exposure:** Vertrautheit allein erhöht tendenziell die Sympathie, besonders bei Dingen, denen wir anfangs neutral gegenüberstehen.

segments.src: 2. **Wear-in → wear-out:** Repetition helps at first, then levels off, and can backfire through boredom and irritation. Varying the ad slows this down.
segments.tr: 2. **Wear-in → Wear-out:** Wiederholung hilft zunächst, flacht dann ab und kann durch Langeweile und Ärger ins Gegenteil umschlagen. Variierte Werbung verlangsamt das.

segments.src: 3. **Ad avoidance:** People avoid ads mentally, emotionally, and physically, most of all when ads are intrusive, frequent, or irrelevant.
segments.tr: 3. **Werbevermeidung:** Menschen vermeiden Werbung gedanklich, emotional und körperlich, am meisten, wenn sie aufdringlich, häufig oder irrelevant ist.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Begriffe des Tages

segments.src: - **Mere exposure effect:** The tendency to like something more simply because you've been exposed to it repeatedly.
segments.tr: - **Mere-Exposure-Effekt:** Die Tendenz, etwas allein deshalb lieber zu mögen, weil man ihm wiederholt ausgesetzt war.

segments.src: - **Processing fluency:** How easily the brain takes in information. Easy processing often feels pleasant and familiar.
segments.tr: - **Verarbeitungsflüssigkeit (Processing Fluency):** Wie leicht das Gehirn Informationen aufnimmt. Leichte Verarbeitung fühlt sich oft angenehm und vertraut an.

segments.src: - **Wear-in / wear-out:** The early stage in which repetition makes an ad more effective, and the later stage in which more repetition reduces its effectiveness.
segments.tr: - **Wear-in / Wear-out:** Die frühe Phase, in der Wiederholung eine Werbung wirksamer macht, und die spätere Phase, in der weitere Wiederholung ihre Wirkung verringert.

segments.src: - **Ad avoidance:** Anything consumers do to reduce their exposure to ads, whether cognitive (ignoring), affective (disliking), or behavioral (skipping or blocking).
segments.tr: - **Werbevermeidung:** Alles, was Konsumenten tun, um ihren Kontakt mit Werbung zu verringern, sei es kognitiv (ignorieren), affektiv (ablehnen) oder verhaltensbezogen (überspringen oder blockieren).

segments.src: - **Frequency cap:** A limit on how many times the same person is shown a particular ad within a set time period.
segments.tr: - **Frequenzbegrenzung (Frequency Cap):** Eine Grenze dafür, wie oft dieselbe Person innerhalb eines bestimmten Zeitraums eine bestimmte Werbung zu sehen bekommt.
